interface.title: pH Diagrams (Streamlit app, chicolucio/pH-diagrams)
interface.stage_of_work: Teaching and exploratory modelling before an experiment (choosing buffers, predicting speciation and titration landmarks)
interface.what_it_is_for: Set up to four pKa values and a total concentration for an acid with sidebar sliders, then view its fractional composition (alpha) diagram and pH-log c (pC) diagram side by side as interactive Plotly charts.

data.note: Nothing is uploaded or loaded. The model is built entirely from slider values: pKa1–pKa4 run 0–14 in steps of 0.5, and concentration runs from 1e-05 to 0.1 M in one-decade steps. The app keeps pKa values from pKa1 up to the first one that breaks non-decreasing order (src/helpers.py valid_pka_values, as the reviewer read it in the source). A 0 that follows a larger pKa therefore drops that step and every later one, but a leading 0, or all-zero sliders, become real pKa = 0 steps. In the run, the default (pKa1 = 1.0, others 0) gave HA. Setting pKa2 to 0, or to 3.0 below pKa1 = 4.5, dropped pKa2–pKa4 with no message (screens/033.webp, screens/036.webp). The theory page shows fixed example charts for acetic, fumaric and citric acid.

features.name: Parameter sliders driving two linked model plots
features.general: Enter a small set of ordered model constants and one scale parameter with bounded, stepped sliders. Every change rebuilds the model and redraws two complementary plots at once, and the plot titles name the model size. Constants are kept only up to the first one that breaks ascending order, and the rest are dropped silently.
features.specific: Sidebar sliders pKa1–pKa4 (0–14, step 0.5) and a log-spaced concentration slider (1e-05 to 0.1). Changing any of them rebuilds the Acid object and redraws both the Distribution diagram and the pC diagram, and the titles show HA/H2A/H3A/H4A. Only the leading run of non-decreasing pKa values is used (src/helpers.py valid_pka_values, per the reviewer). A 0 or a smaller value after a larger pKa drops that step and all later ones, with no message. A leading 0 counts as a real pKa of 0.
steps: Drag a pKa slider, or focus it and use arrow, Home or End keys
Watch both diagrams redraw and the acid's name in the title change (HA … H4A); a redraw can lag one step behind
Set further pKa sliders in non-decreasing order to add dissociation steps; a value below the previous pKa (including 0) drops that step and every later one
Step the concentration slider by decades to shift the pC diagram
serves_tasks: Model a monoprotic acid and see where its two forms are equal
Add dissociation steps one at a time to build a polyprotic acid
Set up a realistic triprotic acid (phosphoric-acid-like)
Compare a diprotic acid whose constants are close together
Dilute the solution and compare the plots

features.name: Reference pH and pOH lines on the log-concentration plot
features.general: Draw the log[H+] and log[OH-] diagonals on the log-concentration plot as guides. The pH of a solution is read where a diagonal intersects the right species curve.
features.specific: The pC diagram draws pH and pOH lines with their own legend entries. Where A- meets the pH line gives the pH of the acid solution, and where HA meets the pOH line gives the pH of the conjugate-base solution. In the replay the lines themselves showed no tooltip; the value is read from the species curve at the crossing.
steps: Find where the pH line crosses the conjugate-base curve and hover there to read the acid solution's pH
Find where the pOH line crosses the acid curve and hover there to read the conjugate-base solution's pH
Turn on spike lines to project the crossing onto the axes
serves_tasks: Estimate the pH of the acid solution and of its conjugate-base solution (≈ equivalence-point pH)

features.name: Hover readout with compare mode and spike lines
features.general: Read exact x/y values off curves by hovering. Switch to compare mode to see every series at the same x, and add spike lines to project the point onto the axes. Use it to find crossings and intersections.
features.specific: Plotly mode bar on each diagram. The app's config adds 'Compare data on hover' and 'Toggle Spike Lines' next to 'Show closest data on hover'. Tooltips show pH and α, or pH and logC, for each species. Compare mode resets when the chart is rebuilt.
steps: Hover near a curve to get the closest point (pH, α or logC)
Click 'Compare data on hover' to list every species at that pH
Click 'Toggle Spike Lines' to drop guides to the axes
Hover at a crossing to read the equivalence point or the solution pH
serves_tasks: Read the crossing point of two species
Estimate the pH of the acid solution and of its conjugate-base solution (≈ equivalence-point pH)
Read the equivalence point and buffer region of a polyprotic acid

features.name: Plot navigation: box zoom, pan, autoscale
features.general: Drag a box to magnify a region of a plot, pan across it, then return to the full view with Autoscale or a double-click.
features.specific: On either diagram, Zoom is the default drag mode; Pan is in the mode bar, and the app's config leaves out the zoom-in/zoom-out buttons. Autoscale or a double-click on the plot restores 0–14 pH.
steps: Drag a box over the region of interest
Switch to Pan and drag to move along pH
Click Autoscale, or double-click the plot, to reset
serves_tasks: Magnify and move around a region of a plot
Read the equivalence point and buffer region of a polyprotic acid

features.name: Interactive legend series toggling
features.general: Hide one series with a single click on its legend entry, show only one series with a double-click, and double-click again to bring all back.
features.specific: Legend entries for species (HA, A-, H2A …) and the pH and pOH reference lines on the pC diagram.
steps: Click a legend entry to hide that curve

Double-click again to restore all curves
